  Exam Date & Time: 17-Nov-2025 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  FIFTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE EXAMINATIONS - NOVEMBER 2025  
  SUBJECT: ICT 3122/IT_3122 PRINCIPLES OF OPERATING SYSTEMS  
  (SPL: INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY)  
  PRINCIPLES OF OPERATING SYSTEMS [ICT 3122]  
  Marks: 50                                                                               Duration: 180 mins.  
  A  
  Answer all the questions.  
  1A)          Two processes are trying to enter their critical sections simultaneously using Dekker's  
  Version 3 algorithm. Apply the algorithm's logic to explain why a deadlock can occur in (5)  
  this situation. Write the supporting pseudocode to justify your answer.  
  
  1B)                Your college must launch a student coding portal within one week. Usage will be low  
  most days but surge during exams. The team wants to avoid buying servers, keep  
  operations minimal, and pay only for what is used.  
  i) Choose an environment category for deployment (e.g., on-premises data center,  
  hosted/on-demand provider, or a mix).                                                       (3)  
  ii) Choose a service option: a fully managed application platform, self-managed virtual  
  machines, or a ready-made application subscription.  
  iii) Identify the network type that can be used by the college. Justify your choices.  
  
  1C)                In a multi-programmed operating system, several processes frequently request access to  
  shared resources such as printers, disk drives, and memory. Occasionally, some  
  processes get stuck indefinitely because each process is holding one resource and  
  waiting for another that is already held by another process. This situation leads to a (2)  
  deadlock, where none of the involved process can proceed. Apply the three deadlock-  
  handling methods to the given scenario for handling deadlocks.  
  
  2A)                Consider the following reference string for a demand-paged system: Reference String :  
  1, 2, 3, 4, 2, 1, 5, 6, 2, 1, 2, 3, 7, 6, 3, 2, 1, 2, 3, 6.  
  i) Illustrate Belady's Anomaly using the given reference string and show step-by-step  
  page replacement, when the number of free frames in the memory are three and four.  
  ii) What are the problems associated with LRU page replacement algorithm? Justify           (5)  
  with an example.  
  iii) Analyze the effect of increasing the degree of multiprogramming beyond a certain  
  limit in a demand-paged system?  
  
  2B)                Apply your understanding of Linux system structure to explain how a user program  
  reads a file from disk, detailing the roles of system libraries, the kernel, and system     (3)  
  utilities in this operation.  
  
  2C)                A video rendering process is executing on the CPU. When it's time quantum expires, the  
  CPU scheduler preempts it and moves another process to the CPU. Identify the new  
  state of the video rendering process after preemption and illustrate this transition using a (2)  
  process state diagram.  
  
  3A)                A system has four processes (P₁, P₂, P₃, P₄) and four resources (R₁, R₂, R₃, R₄). Each      (5)  
  process currently holds and requests certain resources as shown in Table Q. 3A.

  Using this information, analyze the following situations:  
  i) Construct a Wait-For Graph (WFG) for the given system and identify all the  
  deadlocked processes.  
  ii) Suggest the minimal resource or edge change that would break the deadlock without  
  terminating all processes. Specify which process or resource should be altered and why.  
  
  3B)                Consider the exponential average formula used to predict the length of the next CPU  
  burst.  
  a) What are the implications of assigning the following values to the parameters used by  
  the algorithm?  
  $$i) \alpha = 0 and τ = 100 milliseconds$$  
  (3)  
  $$ii) \alpha  = 0.99 and τ = 10 milliseconds$$  
  b) Given the following sequence of CPU-burst times, use the exponential average  
  formula to predict the length of the next CPU burst. Assume τ₀ = 10 ms and α = 0.5.  
  CPU burst (ti) : 8 6 8 6 15 15 15  
  
  3C)                A system has 𝑚=200 physical frames, the OS reserves 8 frames; the remaining are  
  available to 5 user processes with the following sizes:𝑠1=65, 𝑠2=140, 𝑠3=85, 𝑠4=210,  
  $$𝑠5=100                                                                                    (2)$$  
  a) Compute the frame allocation for each process using proportional allocation.  
  b) How equal allocation may impact system performance in this case.  
  
  4A)                A process consists of three memory segments: a Code segment of 1000 bytes, a Data  
  segment of 500 bytes, and a Stack segment of 200 bytes. The available memory blocks  
  in the system are of the following sizes: Block 1 has 1200 bytes, Block 2 has 800 bytes,  
  and Block 3 has 500 bytes.  
  i) Apply segmentation allocation to assign each segment to a suitable memory block.  
  ii) Compute the external fragmentation resulting from this allocation.  
  iii) If the system uses first-fit allocation strategy, explain how the segments would be (5)  
  placed.  
  iv) If the system uses best-fit allocation strategy, explain how the segments would be  
  placed.  
  v) Suppose a new segment of 600 bytes needs to be added. Can it be allocated? If yes, to  
  which block? If not, explain why.  
  
  4B)                Apply the C-SCAN, LOOK and SSTF disk scheduling algorithm to the following  
  sequence of disk requests: 182, 270, 43, 140, 24, 16, 290. Assume the disk is moving  
  towards higher cylinders. The disk head starts at position 150. Show the schematic      (3)  
  representation and calculate the total head movement. Analyse which algorithm is better  
  for uniformly distributed requests.  
  
  4C)                Identify real-world applications that typically use sequential access or random access.  
  Justify your answer.  
  i) Media player  
  ii) Database management system                                                            (2)  
  iii) Log file analyzer  
  iv) Compiler intermediate file

  5A)                  Consider a computer system that uses demand paging. The memory access time is 100  
  nanoseconds, and the page fault service time is 8 milliseconds. In this system, 80  
  percent of the time the replaced pages are not modified and take 6 milliseconds to  
  service, while the remaining 20 percent are modified and require 10 milliseconds to  
  service. The page-fault rate (p) is 0.002, corresponding to 0.2 percent.  
  List and briefly describe the steps involved in handling a page fault in a demand-paging (5)  
  system.  
  Compute the average page fault service time considering both modified and unmodified  
  pages.  
  Using your result from (b), calculate the Effective Access Time (EAT). Then, evaluate  
  whether this system's performance is acceptable if the target EAT ≤ 200 nanoseconds.  
  
  5B)                  Given the following tasks as shown in Table Q. 5B:  
  
  
  (3)  
  i) Compute the CPU utilization for both the Rate-Monotonic Scheduling (RMS) and  
  Earliest-Deadline-First (EDF) algorithms.  
  ii) Identify the scheduling approach that provides a better real-time guarantee for this  
  task set.  
  
  5C)                  A factory automation system must control robotic arms with strict timing, a temperature-  
  monitoring system that can occasionally delay updates, and a reporting module that logs  
  data once per minute. Classify each module as hard, firm, or soft real-time, and justify (2)  
  your classification based on timing and scheduling requirements.
